instrument: FILL IN: <set name> (clone) / all surviving tracks
capture_track: FILL IN: index of the reused capture audio track

track_selection.enumerate: song.tracks (0-based; song.master_track and song.return_tracks are never enumerated)
skip: no arrangement content and no session-clip content (empty)
group/folder tracks (bus sum of already-captured children)

playback_source: the set's own arrangement, song.current_song_time = 0.0 to song.last_event_time, song.loop = 0 (NOT a synthetic session-clip loop)
bounce_length: song.last_event_time converted to seconds at song.tempo, plus settle_seconds tail
purpose: Give the lab a true multitrack (never separated) instead of the Demucs-guessed drums.wav/bass.wav pairs corpus2/band_pump.py currently reads, so pump-depth and band-share numbers can be checked against ground truth for at least one set.
hypothesis: H34 (band-split sidechain duck deeper in sub than low) is currently 'not supported' on Demucs-separated corpus stems (median sub-minus-low pump -0.2 dB). On a real, unseparated kick/bass pair from this set, either the split duck appears clearly (H34's corpus verdict is a separator artifact) or it does not (the technique is genuinely rare/absent in practice, not just hidden by Demucs).
sidecar_note: sample_rate is read from the bounced wav file after the copy, not queried from Live. No 'measure' field: measurement happens out-of-band in the lab, same as the sweep seam.

restore.capture_track_arm: 0 (disarm at end, same as run_sweep_stem.py's finally block)
restore.capture_track_input_routing: left as last set; harmless on a disposable clone

lab_ingest_layout: lab/runner.py --local expects this folder to land at <local_src>/stems/<song-slug>/*.wav (see lab/runner.py run_local docstring)
reuses_mechanism: code/run_sweep_stem.py (ensure_capture_track / bounce_stem), adapted to play the real arrangement once per surviving track instead of a synthetic session-clip loop
